newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - ITALY - FRIDAY JULY 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - ITALY - FRIDAY JULY 4.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimo D'Alema harshly criticised his party allies' stand during talks of held by the parliamentary reforms commission aimed at carrying out constitutional reforms, saying he had been isolated (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi first said Italy's target to join the first wave of European monetary union (EMU) was "within reach", yet efforts must carry on (all).

* Hard left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said he was harshly against the idea of U.S. Telecoms group AT&T becoming a stable shareholder in Italian state telecoms holding STET (all).
* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed retail sales of medium and large firms in Italy rose 1.8 percent in March 1997 compared with a year earlier (Sole 24 Ore).

* Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani, after meeting Olivetti's managing director Roberto Colaninno and trade unions' representatives, said the government would do its best to help Olivetti PC unit find the most suitable financial partners (all).

* Trasport minister Claudio Burlando said the government would approve a financing programme for state railway company Ferrovie dello Stato by the end of July. The plan would include financing for 6.5 trillion lire in 1998/1999 (all).

* Pietro Giudano, finance director of mobile phone operator Omnitel, in which information technology group Olivetti has a dominant stake, said the company had been running an operating profit since April this year. Omnitel also said it had renegatiated an existing 10-year project financing facilitiy of 1.8 trillion lire, raising the amount to 2.8 trillion lire (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
